persona.role: Music industry worker and aspiring writer

sent_to_model:
i want to put together a post for my blog about where i'm at lately. i'm still completely wrapped up in music, but keeping up with everything costs money and energy i don't really have right now. wanting to go to lollapalooza has brought that home. can you help me get these thoughts into a few paragraphs about why i'm easing up on going out, and how my regular job fits into all this music stuff? i'm also feeling discouraged about writing and the opportunities available when your interests aren't commercial. i want people reading my blog to understand why i stick with the projects i care about, even when there's hardly any money in them.

- Have a full-time job alongside music industry work.
- Available creative opportunities tend to be indie projects with little funding.
- Previously interned at entertainment weekly.
- Been living in new york for 7 years.
- Want to attend lollapalooza, especially for moz and the pixies.
- Tickets would cost about $90; travel would be an additional expense.
- Festival would mean missing two workdays.
- Usually keep concert outings local and relatively small.
- Current finances are tight; free activities have particular appeal.
- Going to shows has become tiring.
- Recently tend to pass on concerts without guest-list admission.
- entertainment weekly internship clarified how little most mainstream entertainment appeals to me.
- Music industry effort doesn't seem to provide enough income to support participating fully.
- Envious of people whose parents finance their freedom; combining employment and music commitments feels difficult in this economy.
- Still interested in becoming a writer, though other people's opportunities can feel out of reach.
- Non-mainstream preferences seem to narrow my opportunities; commercial entertainment often feels artificial and insufficiently unfiltered.
- Believe in my projects and endorsements; popularity and fashionable attention aren't sufficient reasons to support something.
- Missing the festival would be disappointing; really eager to see those performers.
- Music matters enormously to me, but frequent big events are expensive.
- Recent years have been very busy; increasingly drawn to a quieter pace.
- Fewer things motivate me to get out lately; wasn't always so selective about experiences.
- Readers should understand the financial and practical reasons for cutting back.
- Readers should recognize personal conviction behind my writing and music interests, rather than assume promotional motives.

(About me: Music industry worker and aspiring writer, New York, US. Length: it should come to roughly 400-800 words.)

must_cover: Money and exhaustion are prompting a slower social life despite continued enthusiasm for music.
Attending lollapalooza presents practical and financial obstacles.
A full-time job supports involvement in music that does not pay enough.
The writer feels discouraged about writing because noncommercial interests limit opportunities, but personal belief drives the projects they support.

reference.kind: a real piece of writing by a real person
